patch.value: A defect the tracker considers closed keeps blocking releases: nothing joins a closed item to the observability issue whose rolling window gates the cut

The release gate reads a rolling 14-day activity window over unresolved observability issues, so an error stops blocking a cut only when someone dispositions it in the external system. Nothing joins the two records. Closing the pm item that owns a defect has no effect on the issue that gates the release, and resolving the issue leaves no trace in the immutable record, so the tracker can report a defect fixed while the release stays red for that same defect, and it can report a defect open while the release is green because the window rolled past it. Measured 2026-08-07: the scheduled cut failed on exactly one blocking issue whose product behaviour was correct, and after the product fix landed the cut still required a manual disposition in a system this repository never writes to. The pieces to close the loop already exist and are unused. The release workflow creates a release object and associates commits with it, so resolve-in-next-release is semantically available; the handled-error channel already tags every event with the error code; and items already carry the observability short identifier in their titles. What is missing is the relation and the automation over it: no dependency kind, no field, and no gate connects a tracked defect to the observability record whose lifetime gates the release. This is a broken turn of the self-improvement loop, because the loop cannot re-measure an improvement whose gate lives outside the record.

A tracked defect and the observability issue that gates the release are joined by a recorded relation, so the join is readable from the immutable record rather than from a title substring; Closing the owning item dispositions the joined observability issue, and the disposition is recorded as a mutation rather than performed silently out of band; The release gate reports, for every blocking issue, whether a tracked item claims to have fixed it, so a red cut names the item that disagrees with it; A negative control proves an unjoined blocking issue still fails the gate, so the join can never be used to waive an untracked error
